description.narrative: (Burundi): Tubiteho, receives Malaria, Maternal Child Health (MCH), and Family Planning (FP) funds and it targets 16 districts in six provinces (390 facilities) and works at the facility and community level. FY22 malaria funds will improve malaria prevention and treatment among pregnant women and children under-five by promoting the routine distribution and use of ITNs during ante-natal care (ANC) and immunization visits. The quality of case management at the facility and community levels will be strengthened. Social and behavior change will focus on early care seeking and proper use of bed nets. FY22 MCH funds will improve access and quality of MCH services and strengthen the capacity of health district teams and health providers to improve oversight and quality of treatment: to integrate and scale-up high-impact interventions, to provide key medical equipment, to integrate the prevention of Mother-To-Child [HIV] Transmission (PMTCT) with MCH services, and to build the capacity of community health workers (CHWs) to carry out SBC interventions, monitoring ANC and delivery at the clinical level with skilled birth attendants, and community maternal death. Integrated Community Case Management (ICCM) will focus on the prevention and treatment of malaria, diarrhea, pneumonia, and FP to reduce their burden on child morbidity and mortality.
